mainTopic: מוסף for an individual, forgetting ראש חודש, the end of תפלת השחר, and the new chapter's demand for כובד ראש in תפילה and restrained joy
overview: The amud opens by finishing שמואל's testimony. He said מוסף alone only once, on the day the king's army came to נהרדעא and there was no חבר עיר. רבי ינאי rejects the ruling that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. רבי יוחנן testifies that he saw רבי ינאי pray twice. On the other side, רב rules like רבי יהודה. When רבי חייא בר אבא prays twice, רבי זירא asks why. The answer is that an individual who forgets ראש חודש must repeat the prayer, because the ברייתא that exempts him speaks only of a צבור. The גמרא then discusses how long to wait between prayers, and rules that forgetting ראש חודש in ערבית never requires repeating, whether the month is full or short. With הדרן the chapter תפלת השחר ends. A new משנה requires praying with כובד ראש and without interruption. The גמרא tests several פסוקים as the source, accepts 'עבדו את ה׳ ביראה', and tells stories about joy that must be mixed with trembling. The last story, about מר בריה דרבינא's wedding, continues on the next amud.

steps.title: שמואל's one exception: the day the king's army came
steps.stepSummary: שמואל finishes his testimony. He never said מוסף alone in נהרדעא except once, when the king's army came to the city and the Sages could not pray together. On that day he prayed alone and was not part of a חבר עיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: [I never prayed מוסף as an individual] in נהרדעא, except for that one day when the king's army came to the city. The Rabbis were busy and upset and did not pray, so I prayed alone, and I was an individual without a חבר עיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing שמואל's statement, which began on the previous amud. He says he prayed מוסף alone only once, on a day of emergency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that שמואל normally prayed מוסף only with the community. The one time he said it alone, there was no חבר עיר at all. This shows he acted like רבי יהודה, who said in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה that מוסף belongs to the community setting.

keyTerms.meaning: Neharde'a, שמואל's city in Babylonia, home to a large Jewish community
they were busy, distracted, or troubled
an organized community prayer group of the town

steps.confusionAlert: This line begins in the middle of a sentence. The first part, 'I never prayed מוסף as an individual,' appears on the previous amud. The word בִּנְהַרְדְּעָא continues שמואל's statement. It does not start a new idea.

phrases.english: in Neharde'a, except for that day
phrases.notes: Continues שמואל's sentence on the previous amud

phrases.english: when the king's army came to the city,
and the Rabbis were preoccupied and did not pray,
and I prayed as an individual,
and I was an individual not in a community prayer group.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְבַר מֵהָהוּא יוֹמָא דַּאֲתָא פּוּלְמוּסָא דְמַלְכָּא לְמָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes שמואל's testimony, which began on the previous amud
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל said מוסף alone only when no חבר עיר existed. This matches רבי יהודה's view.

steps.title: רבי חנינא קרא rules like רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא קרא, the Bible expert, sat before רבי ינאי and declared that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא קרא sat before רבי ינאי, and he sat and said: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה, who said it in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.whatsHappening: A scholar announces a ruling: the הלכה is that מוסף is said only within a חבר עיר. This sets up רבי ינאי's sharp response in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the view of רבי יהודה has support from שמואל's practice. Now someone states it as the actual הלכה. That raises the question of whether the halachic authorities in ארץ ישראל accept it.

keyTerms.meaning: a Bible expert, someone who reads and teaches the verses
the law follows the opinion of...

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina the Bible expert sat
before Rabbi Yannai,
and he sat and was saying:
The halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה.
phrases.english: who said it in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה שֶׁאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns שמואל's practice into a stated הלכה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנינא קרא holds that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה: מוסף is only for a חבר עיר.

steps.title: רבי ינאי rejects the ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי tells רבי חנינא קרא to go read his verses outside, because the הלכה does not follow רבי יהודה in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Go read your verses outside, because the הלכה does not follow רבי יהודה, who said it in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ינאי firmly rejects the ruling from the previous step. He says the הלכה is not like רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'go read your verses outside' is a sharp put-down. It means a ruling like this has no place in the בית מדרש. The practical result is that an individual must say מוסף even without a חבר עיר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the accepted practice that every individual says מוסף, even when praying alone.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: פּוּק קְרֵא קְרָאָיךְ לְבָרָא,
phrases.english: He said to him: Go out and read your verses outside,
for the halakha does not follow Rabbi Yehuda

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה.
phrases.english: who said it in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya.

steps.triggerLanguage: פּוּק קְרֵא קְרָאָיךְ לְבָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly rejects רבי חנינא קרא's ruling
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole ruling that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ruling is simply not the accepted הלכה. An individual must say מוסף.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן saw רבי ינאי pray twice
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן testifies that he saw רבי ינאי pray and then pray again. This is understood as שחרית followed by מוסף, said as an individual.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: I saw רבי ינאי pray, and then pray again.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן brings an eyewitness report. It shows that רבי ינאי himself followed his own ruling and said מוסף alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי ינאי prayed a second תפילה right after the first, the natural reading is that the second was מוסף. That would prove in practice that he holds an individual must say מוסף.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
I saw Rabbi Yannai
who prayed and then prayed again.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲנִי רָאִיתִי אֶת רַבִּי יַנַּאי דְּצַלִּי וַהֲדַר צַלִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי ינאי's ruling with his own conduct
steps.raayaObject: That an individual must say מוסף, as רבי ינאי ruled
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's eyewitness testimony that רבי ינאי prayed twice

steps.title: Maybe the second prayer was for better concentration
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה suggests to רבי זירא another reading. Perhaps רבי ינאי lacked כוונה the first time and repeated שחרית with proper focus, so the second prayer was not מוסף at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said to רבי זירא: Maybe at first he did not focus his mind, and in the end he did focus his mind.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה pushes back on the proof from the previous step. He offers another explanation for why רבי ינאי prayed twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works only if the second prayer was מוסף. If רבי ינאי was just repeating שחרית because he lacked כוונה, the story proves nothing about מוסף for an individual.

keyTerms.meaning: he focused his mind, had proper כוונה

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לְרַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said to Rabbi Zeira:
But perhaps initially he did not focus his mind
and ultimately he focused his mind.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִילְמָא מֵעִיקָּרָא לָא כַּוֵּון דַּעְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the meaning of the proof in step 4
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The assumption that the second prayer was מוסף
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The second prayer could have been a repeat of שחרית for כוונה

steps.title: Look at how great the witness is
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that the witness is רבי יוחנן, a great man. He would not report this story as meaningful unless he knew the second prayer was מוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: See who the great man is who testifies about him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא defends the proof against רבי ירמיה's doubt. He points to the reliability of the witness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא does not argue about כוונה at all. He relies on רבי יוחנן's stature: a great witness would have noticed the difference and would only tell the story if it showed מוסף. The proof therefore stands.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי ינאי ruled that the הלכה is not like רבי יהודה in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, so even an individual must say מוסף. רבי יוחנן's testimony about his practice stands. Step 8 brings an opposing ruling in the name of רב.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲזִי מַאן גַּבְרָא רַבָּה
phrases.english: He said to him: See who the great man is
who is testifying about him.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲזִי מַאן גַּבְרָא רַבָּה דְּקָמַסְהֵיד עֲלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי ירמיה's challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The double prayer might have been a repeat for כוונה
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן would only testify about it if it was מוסף, so the proof stands

steps.title: רבי אמי and רבי אסי prayed where they learned
steps.stepSummary: Even though טבריה had thirteen synagogues, רבי אמי and רבי אסי prayed only between the columns of the place where they studied Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי and רבי אסי, even though they had thirteen synagogues in טבריה, would pray only between the columns, the place where they learned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shifts to a new story about the Sages' prayer: where they chose to pray.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They had many synagogues to choose from, yet they chose the בית מדרש, the place of their learning. This shows how much they valued praying in a place of תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: between the columns (of the study hall)

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi,
even though they had
thirteen synagogues in Tiberias,

phrases.aramaic: לָא הֲווֹ מְצַלּוּ אֶלָּא בֵּינֵי עַמּוּדֵי,
phrases.english: would pray only between the columns,
where they would study.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי אַף עַל גַּב דַּהֲווֹ לְהוּ תְּלֵיסַר בֵּי כְנִישְׁתָּא בִּטְבֶרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story on the related theme of the Sages' prayer practices
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Sages preferred to pray in their place of Torah study over the many synagogues.

steps.title: A different ruling about individual prayer
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר אבדימי reports that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה's statement in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב יצחק בר אבדימי said in the name of our teacher that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, who spoke in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now reports a ruling that differs from the ruling attributed to רבי ינאי earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier ruling rejected following רבי יהודה on the question of an individual's מוסף. This statement says to follow him, so the גמרא has placed two different rulings before us.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of; citing someone.

phrases.english: It was stated: Rav Yitzḥak bar Avdimi

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם רַבֵּינוּ אָמַר: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: said in the name of our teacher: The law follows Rabbi Yehuda

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה.
phrases.english: who spoke in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר, רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the account of רבי אמי and רבי אסי to the earlier dispute about an individual's מוסף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה's statement in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

steps.title: Why did he pray twice?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא prays twice, and רבי זירא asks why.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא prayed and then prayed again. רבי זירא asked him, “Why did you do that?”
steps.whatsHappening: A new incident introduces two consecutive prayers. רבי זירא asks for the reason, setting up the explanations that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the ruling just cited in step 8, an individual does not say מוסף, so the second prayer could not have been מוסף. רבי זירא therefore asks what other reason made a second prayer necessary.

keyTerms.meaning: A respectful way to address someone: master or sir.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא צַלִּי וַהֲדַר צַלִּי.
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba prayed and then prayed again.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא: מַאי טַעְמָא עָבֵיד מָר הָכִי?
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to him: Why did you do this?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא: מַאי טַעְמָא עָבֵיד מָר הָכִי?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows רב's ruling in step 8. If an individual does not say מוסף, the second prayer of רבי חייא בר אבא cannot have been מוסף, so רבי זירא asks why he prayed again.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why did רבי חייא בר אבא pray a second time?

steps.title: Poor focus does not explain the second prayer
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא considers whether the first prayer lacked focus, then cites רבי אליעזר's instruction to assess one's ability to focus before praying.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the reason was that you could not focus, רבי אליעזר said that a person should assess himself: if he can focus his heart, he should pray; if not, he should not pray.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא tests one possible explanation for the repeated prayer and pushes it aside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He suggests that רבי חייא בר אבא may have repeated the prayer because he lacked כוונה the first time. But the teaching of רבי אליעזר says to check one's ability to focus before beginning, so רבי זירא looks for another reason.

phrases.aramaic: אִילֵּימָא מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא כַּוֵּון מָר דַּעְתֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: If you say it was because you did not focus your mind,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: לְעוֹלָם יָמוֹד אָדָם אֶת עַצְמוֹ,
phrases.english: but didn't Rabbi Eliezer say: A person should always assess himself:

phrases.aramaic: אִם יָכוֹל לְכַוֵּין אֶת לִבּוֹ — יִתְפַּלֵּל,
phrases.english: if he can focus his heart, he should pray,
and if not, he should not pray.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא כַּוֵּון מָר דַּעְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests a possible answer to רבי זירא's question.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that lack of focus explains the second prayer.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי אליעזר's teaching calls for assessing one's ability to focus before praying.

steps.title: Perhaps he omitted the mention of ראש חודש
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא proposes that רבי חייא בר אבא prayed again because he omitted the mention of ראש חודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, you did not mention ראש חודש.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא offers a different reason for the second prayer: the first prayer omitted ראש חודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This changes the issue from the person's focus to words missing from the prayer. The next step will test whether that omission actually requires repetition.

keyTerms.meaning: Of the New Moon; referring to ראש חודש.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא דְּלָא אַדְכַּר מָר דְּרֵישׁ יַרְחָא.
phrases.english: Rather, you did not mention the New Moon.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּלָא אַדְכַּר מָר דְּרֵישׁ יַרְחָא.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected explanation based on focus with an explanation based on omission.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי חייא בר אבא repeated the prayer because he had omitted the mention of ראש חודש.

steps.title: A teaching says not to repeat for that omission
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that someone who omits ראש חודש in several prayers is not made to repeat, because another prayer remains in which to mention it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught: If someone forgot to mention ראש חודש in ערבית, he is not made to repeat it, because he can say it in שחרית. The same applies from שחרית to מוסף, and from מוסף to מנחה.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא challenges רבי זירא's new explanation. It says that an omitted mention of ראש חודש does not require repetition in the cases it lists.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives a reason each time: another prayer is coming. If its rule applies to רבי חייא בר אבא, his omission would not explain why he prayed again.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught? Introduces a challenge from a teaching.
Require someone to go back and repeat.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא טָעָה וְלֹא הִזְכִּיר שֶׁל רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: If someone erred and did not mention the New Moon,
in the evening prayer, he is not made to repeat it,
because he can say it in the morning prayer.
In the morning prayer, he is not made to repeat it,
because he can say it in the additional prayer.
In the additional prayer, he is not made to repeat it,
because he can say it in the afternoon prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא טָעָה וְלֹא הִזְכִּיר שֶׁל רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim that omitting ראש חודש explains the repeated prayer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that רבי חייא בר אבא repeated his prayer because he omitted ראש חודש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says not to require repetition for the listed omissions, since the mention can be said in a later prayer.

steps.title: The teaching concerns communal prayer
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא replies that רבי יוחנן limited the ברייתא to prayer in a communal setting.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Wasn't it stated about that teaching that רבי יוחנן said, “They taught it regarding a congregation”?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא answers the challenge by narrowing the ברייתא's rule. According to רבי יוחנן, it was taught about communal prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's exemption remains in place for its communal case. רבי חייא בר אבא's individual prayer is a different case, so the ברייתא does not rule out his need to repeat it.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated about it; a comment was made on that teaching.

steps.whatToRemember: The answer does not discard the ברייתא. It limits its no-repeat rule to prayer בְּצִבּוּר.

phrases.english: He said to him: Wasn't it stated about that teaching
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said: They taught it regarding a congregation?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו אִיתְּמַר עֲלַהּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בְּצִבּוּר שָׁנוּ.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא by identifying the setting to which it applies.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the cited teaching to communal prayer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's no-repeat rule also applies to the individual prayer of רבי חייא בר אבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא was taught about prayer בְּצִבּוּר, so it does not prevent an individual from repeating the prayer.

steps.title: How long should one wait between prayers?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how long to pause between one prayer and the next.
steps.simpleTranslation: How long should one wait between one prayer and another?
steps.whatsHappening: After discussing a repeated prayer, the גמרא turns to a practical follow-up question: how long to wait before the next prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumes that two prayers may be said in succession. It asks about the pause between them, not whether the second prayer is needed.

phrases.english: How long should one wait between one prayer and another?

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּמָּה יִשְׁהֶה בֵּין תְּפִלָּה לִתְפִלָּה?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from why a prayer was repeated to the pause before a second prayer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The required waiting time between consecutive prayers.

steps.title: Wait until the mind is ready to pray again
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא and רב חסדא give two formulations: wait until one's mind is ready to plead, or until it is ready to beseech.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא and רב חסדא: one said to wait until his mind is ready to plead; the other said to wait until his mind is ready to beseech.
steps.whatsHappening: Two answers describe the pause by the person's readiness to pray again. The text does not say which of the two named teachers gave which wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither answer gives a number of minutes. Both describe the state of mind needed before beginning the next prayer.

keyTerms.meaning: That it becomes ready to plead.
That it becomes ready to beseech.

steps.whatToRemember: The answer gives a measure of readiness, not a fixed time.

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא וְרַב חִסְדָּא. חַד אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Huna and Rav Ḥisda: one said,
long enough for his mind to become ready to plead,

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: כְּדֵי שֶׁתִּתְחוֹלֵל דַּעְתּוֹ עָלָיו.
phrases.english: and the other said: long enough for his mind to become ready to beseech.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא וְרַב חִסְדָּא. חַד אָמַר: כְּדֵי שֶׁתִּתְחוֹנֵן דַּעְתּוֹ עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the pause between prayers.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Wait until one's mind is ready for a fresh prayer, described with two closely related expressions.

steps.title: A verse for each description of the pause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא connects each description of readiness to pray with a verse about משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who said to wait until the mind is ready to plead relies on “And I pleaded before the Lord.” The one who said to wait until the mind is ready to beseech relies on “And משה besought.”
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is explaining the two wordings given in the previous step. It shows where each wording comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One verse uses language resembling תִּתְחוֹנֵן; the other uses language resembling תִּתְחוֹלֵל. This step does not choose between the two views.

phrases.english: The one who said, “Until his mind is ready to plead,”
bases it on what is written: “And I pleaded before the Lord.”
And the one who said, “Until his mind is ready to beseech,”
bases it on what is written: “And Moses besought.”

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר ״כְּדֵי שֶׁתִּתְחוֹנֵן דַּעְתּוֹ עָלָיו״, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a verse for each of the two formulations in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: The wording of each view about readiness for the next prayer.

steps.title: An evening omission does not require repetition
steps.stepSummary: רב says that omitting ראש חודש from the evening prayer does not require repeating it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ענן said in the name of רב: If someone erred and did not mention ראש חודש in the evening prayer, we do not make him repeat it, because בית דין sanctifies the month only during the day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the earlier discussion of a missed ראש חודש mention. רב now gives a rule specifically for the evening prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule rests on a stated reason: בית דין does not sanctify the month at night. Because the reason concerns nighttime, רב says the omission then does not require repetition.

phrases.english: Rav Anan said in the name of Rav:

phrases.aramaic: טָעָה וְלֹא הִזְכִּיר שֶׁל רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ עַרְבִית —
phrases.english: If someone erred and did not mention the New Moon in the evening prayer—
we do not make him repeat it,

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין בֵּית דִּין מְקַדְּשִׁין אֶת הַחֹדֶשׁ אֶלָּא בַּיּוֹם.
phrases.english: because the court sanctifies the month only during the day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב עָנָן אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the pause-between-prayers discussion and returns to the earlier ראש חודש omission discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Omitting ראש חודש in ערבית does not require repeating the prayer, because בית דין sanctifies the month only by day.

steps.title: A proposed limit for a short month
steps.stepSummary: אמימר proposes that רב’s exemption applies to a full month, but not to a short month.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: רב’s statement makes sense for a full month. But for a short month, we make him repeat the prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר narrows רב’s rule. He says that in a short month, an evening omission does require repetition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אמימר distinguishes a month with two days associated with ראש חודש from one with only one. His distinction changes the outcome for the short-month case.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַמֵּימָר: מִסְתַּבְּרָא מִילְּתָא דְּרַב בְּחֹדֶשׁ מָלֵא.
phrases.english: Ameimar said: Rav’s statement is reasonable in a full month.
But in a short month, we make him repeat it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַמֵּימָר: מִסְתַּבְּרָא מִילְּתָא דְּרַב בְּחֹדֶשׁ מָלֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a limit on the nighttime exemption stated in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to אמימר’s proposed distinction, an evening omission requires repetition in a חודש חסר.

steps.title: The stated reason applies to both kinds of month
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges אמימר’s distinction by pointing back to רב’s reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to אמימר: Since רב gave a reason, what difference does it make whether the month is short or full?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי challenges the proposed limit. He asks why month length should matter if רב’s reason is that בית דין acts only during the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A short month does not change when בית דין sanctifies the month. רב אשי is testing אמימר’s distinction against the reason רב himself gave.

keyTerms.meaning: what difference does it make to me?

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Ameimar:
Since Rav stated a reason,

phrases.aramaic: מָה לִי חָסֵר וּמָה לִי מָלֵא?!
phrases.english: what difference does it make whether the month is short or full?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדֵי רַב טַעְמָא קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אמימר’s distinction using the reason stated in רב’s original rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר’s claim that a חודש חסר requires repetition at night.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב’s reason—that בית דין sanctifies the month only by day—applies whether the month is חסר or מלא.

steps.title: Month length makes no difference
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי concludes that the evening rule is the same for both kinds of month.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, there is no difference.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי states the result of his challenge: the proposed distinction does not stand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for רב’s rule is about night versus day, not about month length. Therefore the evening exemption applies in both cases.
steps.whatToRemember: For an omission of ראש חודש in ערבית, רב’s reason applies whether the month is חסר or מלא.

phrases.english: Rather, there is no difference.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָא שְׁנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the conclusion reached from רב אשי’s challenge.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב’s exemption for omitting ראש חודש in ערבית applies to both a חודש חסר and a חודש מלא.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter תפלת השחר
steps.stepSummary: The formal closing line of the fourth chapter of ברכות, תפלת השחר.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'תפלת השחר'.
steps.whatsHappening: This is not an argument. It is the traditional closing line that marks the end of the chapter תפלת השחר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The discussion about ראש חודש in the evening prayer (steps 17-20) was the last topic of this chapter. With this line the chapter is formally finished, and a brand-new chapter with a new topic begins next.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you: the closing formula said at the end of a chapter
The morning prayer; the name of the chapter now ending

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this line as part of the משנה that follows. It belongs to the previous chapter and only marks its end.

phrases.english: We will return to you
phrases.notes: Standard formula for finishing a chapter

phrases.english: 'The Morning Prayer' (chapter name)
phrases.notes: Named after the chapter's opening words

steps.triggerLanguage: הדרן עלך תפלת השחר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formally closes the chapter whose final discussion ended in step 20.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter תפלת השחר is complete. A new chapter begins.

steps.title: The new משנה: praying with seriousness and without interruption
steps.stepSummary: The משנה requires a serious frame of mind before תפילה. It describes how the early pious men prepared for an hour, and it forbids interrupting תפילה even for a king or a snake.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may only stand up to pray with a serious, humble mind. The early pious men would wait one hour and then pray, so that they could focus their hearts toward their Father in Heaven. Even if the king greets a person while he is praying, he should not answer. Even if a snake is wrapped around his heel, he should not stop.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter opens with a משנה about the right mindset for תפילה. It teaches three things: the required seriousness, an example of extra preparation, and the rule against interrupting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic rule is כובד ראש, meaning a heavy, serious mind rather than a light or joking one. The חסידים הראשונים went further and spent a full hour preparing so that their hearts would be focused on ה׳. Since a person praying is standing before ה׳, nothing ordinary may pull him away, not even a human king or a snake.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה: marks the start of the משנה text
Heaviness of head: a serious, humble, focused frame of mind
The early pious men, people who went beyond the basic requirement
So that they would direct (focus) their hearts

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה sets the basic halachic standard for כוונה and for not interrupting the עמידה. It becomes the foundation for the whole chapter's discussion of prayer focus.
steps.confusionAlert: The hour of waiting is described as the practice of the חסידים הראשונים, a level of extra piety. The basic requirement for everyone is כובד ראש, not necessarily a full hour.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One may not stand up to pray
phrases.notes: עומדין refers to standing for the עמידה

phrases.english: except from a state of seriousness (heaviness of head).
phrases.notes: A serious, humble mindset

phrases.english: The early pious men
would wait one hour, and then pray,
so that they would focus their hearts
toward their Father in Heaven.

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ הַמֶּלֶךְ שׁוֹאֵל בִּשְׁלוֹמוֹ — לֹא יְשִׁיבֶנּוּ,
phrases.english: Even if the king greets him, he should not answer him,
phrases.notes: The commentaries limit this to a Jewish king, who would not kill him for ignoring the greeting

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ נָחָשׁ כָּרוּךְ עַל עֲקֵבוֹ — לֹא יַפְסִיק.
phrases.english: and even if a snake is wrapped around his heel, he should not interrupt.
phrases.notes: The גמרא later qualifies this for truly dangerous creatures

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין עוֹמְדִין לְהִתְפַּלֵּל אֶלָּא מִתּוֹךְ כּוֹבֶד רֹאשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter with a new topic right after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תפילה must begin with כובד ראש, and one may not interrupt it even for a king's greeting or a snake on the heel.

steps.title: Asking for the source of the משנה's rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that תפילה requires כובד ראש.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: From where are these things learned?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and immediately asks for the source of the משנה's first rule. This question sets up the next step, where an answer will be offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה stated a rule without giving its source. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches that one must pray with a serious, humble mind.

keyTerms.meaning: Marks the start of the גמרא's discussion
From where are these words (learned)? The standard request for a source

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where are these matters derived?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the scriptural source of the משנה's rule of כובד ראש.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק teaches that one may pray only with כובד ראש?

steps.title: רבי אלעזר brings a source from חנה's prayer
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers that the source is the פסוק describing חנה, 'והיא מרת נפש'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: The source is the פסוק that says, 'And she was bitter of soul.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the question by pointing to the פסוק about חנה, the mother of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before חנה prayed, the פסוק describes her as 'bitter of soul', meaning deeply serious and broken-hearted. רבי אלעזר reads this as the model for how everyone should approach תפילה: with a heavy, humble heart, which is כובד ראש.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who gives the source
And she was bitter of soul (שמואל א א:י, about חנה)

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
As the verse states:
"And she was bitter of soul."
phrases.notes: The verse continues: 'and she prayed to ה׳ and wept'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חנה prayed while 'bitter of soul', which teaches that תפילה requires a serious, humble heart.

steps.title: Maybe חנה was a special case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבי אלעזר's proof. חנה may have prayed that way only because she was truly in deep pain, so her case does not set a rule for everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do you know this? Maybe חנה is different, because her heart was very bitter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי אלעזר's proof and argues that the פסוק may only describe חנה's personal situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק tells us how חנה felt, not how everyone must feel. She had no children and was in great pain, so her bitter heart was a natural result of her life. That does not prove that every person must bring that kind of seriousness to every תפילה.

keyTerms.meaning: From what (do you know)? It questions whether the proof really works

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not disputing the משנה's rule. It agrees that כובד ראש is required and is only rejecting this particular פסוק as the source. It will look for a better one.

phrases.english: From what (is this proven)?
Perhaps Hannah is different,
since her heart was extremely bitter.
phrases.notes: Her personal suffering explains her state of mind

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי? דִּילְמָא חַנָּה שָׁאנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 24.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from חנה, not the משנה's rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: חנה's bitterness came from her personal suffering. Her case is unique and cannot serve as a general requirement for everyone.

steps.title: A second source: דוד enters God's house in awe
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא offers a new source for כובד ראש: דוד says he will bow toward God's holy היכל 'in Your fear'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: we learn it from here: 'And I, through Your great kindness, will come into Your house; I will bow toward Your holy Temple in fear of You.'
steps.whatsHappening: Since the proof from חנה was rejected, the גמרא brings a different פסוק to show that one must pray with awe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא tells us the earlier proof is dropped and a new one replaces it. In this פסוק דוד describes coming before God with יראה. Coming to pray is like entering the בית המקדש, so it must be done with reverence.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the old answer and brings a new one)
In fear or awe of You

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא, מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina said: from here:
"And I, through Your abundant kindness, will enter Your house;
phrases.notes: Psalms 5:8

phrases.english: I will bow toward Your holy Temple in fear of You."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא, מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof from חנה with a new פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is דוד's statement 'אשתחוה אל היכל קדשך ביראתך'.

steps.title: Rejected: דוד was a special case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof because דוד prayed with extra pain and self-affliction, so he is not a model for everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do you know? Perhaps דוד is different, because he used to afflict himself very much in his prayers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from דוד, just as it did with חנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is the same as before: a special person in a special situation cannot set a rule for everyone. דוד pained himself greatly in prayer (Sefaria explains: to gain atonement), so his awe may have been extra and not required of all.

keyTerms.meaning: From what? How do you know? (opens a rejection)

phrases.english: From what do you know this?
Perhaps David is different,
since he would greatly afflict himself in prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי? דִּילְמָא דָּוִד שָׁאנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof given in step 26.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The entire proof from דוד's פסוק
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: דוד's personal practice of extra self-affliction makes him an exception, not a general model.

steps.title: A third source: read 'beauty' as 'trembling'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי brings a general פסוק about bowing to God and rereads בהדרת as בחרדת, trembling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יהושע בן לוי said: we learn it from here: 'Bow to God בהדרת קודש.' Do not read בהדרת (in the beauty of) but בחרדת (in the trembling of).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a third source, this time a פסוק speaking to everyone, not about one person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This avoids the problem of the last two proofs, since the פסוק is a command to all people. Using אל תקרי, the word הדרת (beauty) is reread as חרדת (trembling), teaching that one should pray with holy trembling.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not read (a reading that reshapes a word to teach a lesson)

steps.confusionAlert: אל תקרי does not mean the written פסוק is wrong. It adds a second layer of meaning on top of the plain reading.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי, מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: from here:
"Bow to the Lord in the beauty of holiness."
phrases.notes: Psalms 29:2

phrases.english: Do not read "in the beauty of"
but rather "in the trembling of."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי, מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof from דוד with a general פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is 'השתחוו לה׳ בהדרת קודש', read as בחרדת קודש.

steps.title: Rejected: 'beauty' may mean fine clothing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that הדרת may keep its plain meaning, beauty, teaching that one should dress nicely for תפילה, as רב יהודה did.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do you know? Perhaps I can tell you that it really means 'beauty,' like רב יהודה, who would dress himself up and then pray.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the reread of the פסוק by saying the plain meaning works fine and teaches something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If הדרת means real beauty, the פסוק is about looking dignified before God, not about trembling. רב יהודה's practice of dressing up before praying shows this meaning is real, so the פסוק no longer proves כובד ראש.
steps.whyThisMatters: רב יהודה's practice is a source for wearing nice clothing when standing before God in תפילה.

phrases.english: From what do you know this?
Perhaps, actually, I would tell you,
"beauty" literally.
Like that practice of Rav Yehuda,
who would adorn himself and then pray.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי? דִּילְמָא לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לְךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the אל תקרי reading of step 28.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word can keep its plain meaning of beauty, which points to dressing nicely, not trembling.

steps.title: The accepted source: serve God with fear
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings 'עבדו את ה׳ ביראה וגילו ברעדה', and this source stands unchallenged.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב נחמן בר יצחק said: we learn it from here: 'Serve God with fear, and rejoice with trembling.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a fourth source, and this time it does not reject it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק is a general command, so it is not about one special person. It says יראה openly, so no rereading is needed. Both earlier weaknesses are avoided, and the proof holds.
steps.whatToRemember: After three rejected proofs (חנה, דוד, בהדרת קודש), the source that תפילה needs כובד ראש is 'עבדו את ה׳ ביראה'.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: from here:
"Serve the Lord with fear,
phrases.notes: Psalms 2:11

phrases.english: and rejoice with trembling."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof of step 28 with the final, unchallenged source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is 'עבדו את ה׳ ביראה'.

steps.title: What does 'rejoice with trembling' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how joy and trembling can go together, as the second half of the פסוק says.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'and rejoice with trembling'?
steps.whatsHappening: Having quoted the פסוק, the גמרא stops to ask about its puzzling second half. This sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Joy and trembling seem to be opposite feelings. The question asks for a meaning that lets the two exist together.

phrases.english: What is the meaning of "and rejoice with trembling"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״וְגִילוּ בִּרְעָדָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the פסוק quoted in step 30.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How joy and trembling can go together.

steps.title: Where there is joy, there should be trembling
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר מתנא, quoting רבה, explains that even in a time of joy a person must keep a sense of trembling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר מתנא said in the name of רבה: in a place of rejoicing, there should be trembling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: joy is allowed, but it should never be wild and without awe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two feelings are not opposites here. Joy is fine, but it must be balanced by awe of God. This fits the topic of serious, reverent prayer.
steps.whatToRemember: Joy and awe belong together: even in happy moments a person keeps a sense of trembling before God.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָא אָמַר רַבָּה:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Mattana said in the name of Rabba:
In a place of rejoicing, there should be trembling.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָא אָמַר רַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even where there is joy, trembling must be present.

steps.title: רבה challenges אביי for being very joyful
steps.stepSummary: רבה sees אביי being very happy and quotes 'וגילו ברעדה' (rejoice with trembling) as a challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי was sitting in front of רבה. רבה saw that he was very joyful. He said: It is written, 'Rejoice with trembling'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows the lesson of the last step in real life. רבה sees his student אביי being very happy and challenges him with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה uses the very פסוק that was just explained in step 32: joy must come with trembling. אביי's joy looked unrestrained, with no trembling at all. So רבה challenges him: how can you act this way when the פסוק says to rejoice only with trembling?

keyTerms.meaning: was sitting before him (as a student before a teacher)

steps.confusionAlert: Note that רבה is not saying joy is forbidden. The פסוק itself says 'rejoice.' He is challenging joy that has no trembling mixed in.

phrases.english: Abaye was sitting before Rabba
phrases.notes: רבה was אביי's teacher (and uncle).

phrases.english: He (Rabba) saw that he was very joyful.
phrases.notes: The joy seemed excessive.

phrases.english: He said: It is written, 'Rejoice with trembling'!
phrases.notes: The same פסוק discussed in steps 30-32.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר ״וְגִילוּ בִּרְעָדָה״ כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that applies רבה's rule from step 32 (joy must include trembling) to a real situation.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק requires joy mixed with trembling; אביי's joy seems to have no trembling, so it appears to go against the פסוק.

steps.title: אביי answers that he is wearing תפילין
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that his joy is fine because he is wearing תפילין, which keep the fear of Heaven on him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I am wearing תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers his teacher's challenge. He says his joy is not a problem because he is wearing תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תפילין are a sign of God's presence on a person, so while wearing them a person carries a built-in sense of awe. That awe is the 'trembling' the פסוק demands. So אביי's joy is really joy with trembling, exactly as the פסוק requires.

keyTerms.meaning: I am wearing (literally: I am placing)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the 'trembling' does not have to be a gloomy feeling. A steady reminder of God, like wearing תפילין, is enough to keep joy in proper bounds.

phrases.english: He said to him: I am wearing tefillin.
phrases.notes: The תפילין supply the fear of Heaven, so his joy is not unrestrained.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא תְּפִילִּין מַנַּחְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה's challenge from step 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual answer: the needed trembling is already present through the תפילין.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי's joy has no trembling and goes against 'וגילו ברעדה'.
steps.terutzMaskana: Wearing תפילין keeps awe upon him, so his joy counts as joy with trembling.

steps.title: רבי זירא challenges רבי ירמיה with a פסוק about sorrow
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא sees רבי ירמיה being very happy and quotes 'בכל עצב יהיה מותר' (in all sorrow there is profit) as a challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה was sitting in front of רבי זירא. רבי זירא saw that he was very joyful. He said to him: Is it not written, 'In all sorrow there is profit'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, similar story. This time רבי זירא challenges his student רבי ירמיה for being very happy, using a different פסוק from משלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new פסוק says that some seriousness or sorrow brings benefit to a person. רבי זירא's point is that a person should keep a serious side, not be swept away by joy. It is the same kind of challenge as in step 33, but from a different פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In all sorrow there is profit' (משלי יד:כג)

steps.confusionAlert: Here מוֹתָר means 'profit,' not 'permitted.' Do not read it as the halachic word for 'allowed.'

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה הֲוָה יָתֵיב קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי זֵירָא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya was sitting before Rabbi Zeira.
phrases.notes: רבי זירא is the teacher here.

phrases.english: He (Rabbi Zeira) saw that he was very joyful.
phrases.notes: Same wording as in step 33.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: ״בְּכׇל עֶצֶב יִהְיֶה מוֹתָר״ כְּתִיב?
phrases.english: He said to him: Is it not written, 'In all sorrow there is profit'?
phrases.notes: Proverbs 14:23.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: ״בְּכׇל עֶצֶב יִהְיֶה מוֹתָר״ כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story to step 33, with a different teacher, student, and פסוק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says seriousness brings benefit, so excessive joy seems wrong.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה also answers that he is wearing תפילין
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה gives the same answer as אביי: he is wearing תפילין, so his joy is in proper bounds.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I am wearing תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers his teacher with the exact same words אביי used. His joy is fine because he is wearing תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two stories confirm each other: wearing תפילין brings the needed seriousness and awe. So even great joy is acceptable, because it is never fully free of the fear of Heaven.

keyTerms.meaning: fear of Heaven, awe of God (the idea behind the answer)

steps.whatToRemember: Joy must always come with some trembling or seriousness (רבה, step 32). Wearing תפילין supplies that awe, which is why both אביי and רבי ירמיה could be very joyful while wearing them.

phrases.english: He said to him: I am wearing tefillin.
phrases.notes: The same answer as in step 34.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא תְּפִילִּין מַנַּחְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's challenge from step 35, repeating אביי's answer from step 34.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual answer: the תפילין provide the needed seriousness.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי ירמיה's joy goes against 'בכל עצב יהיה מותר'.
steps.terutzMaskana: While wearing תפילין, a person's joy stays tied to awe of God, so it is acceptable.

steps.title: מר בריה דרבינא sees the רבנן rejoicing too much at his son's wedding
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new story: at his son's wedding feast, מר בריה דרבינא noticed that the רבנן were overly joyous.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר, the son of רבינא, made a wedding feast for his son. He saw that the רבנן were rejoicing excessively.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new story to illustrate the idea of 'rejoice with trembling.' This line only sets the scene. The next line will tell us what מר בריה דרבינא did about the excessive joy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps established that joy must be balanced with fear of Heaven. Here the גמרא brings a real-life case: a wedding, a time when joy is a מצוה. Even so, the word טובא ('excessively') signals that the joy crossed a line, so the host will need to respond.

keyTerms.meaning: מר, the son of רבינא, a later אמורא

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not that the רבנן were happy. Rejoicing at a wedding is a מצוה. The key word is טובא: their joy went beyond proper bounds.

phrases.english: Mar, the son of Ravina,
phrases.notes: The main character of this story

phrases.english: made a wedding feast for his son.
phrases.notes: הילולא here means a wedding celebration

phrases.english: He saw the Sages
phrases.notes: חזנהו = חזא + להו, 'he saw them'

phrases.english: who were rejoicing excessively.
phrases.notes: קבדחי = קא בדחי, 'were being merry.' טובא = too much

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Narrative setup (מעשה) introducing an illustration rather than a legal statement
steps.triggerLanguage: מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבִינָא עֲבַד הִילּוּלָא לִבְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After two stories in which תפילין justified great joy, the גמרא brings another story on the same theme of excessive joy, this time at a wedding.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets the scene: at a wedding feast the רבנן were rejoicing beyond proper bounds, which prepares for the host's response in the next lines.
